data.title: Sporotrichosis — viva
data.summary: Fungal infections · 7 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Sporotrichosis** (Fungal infections)_

**Q1. Causative agent?**
- Sporothrix schenckii complex (S. schenckii, S. brasiliensis, S. globosa — commonest in India) — thermally dimorphic fungus (mould at 25 °C, yeast at 37 °C)

**Q2. Mode of infection and risk groups?**
- Traumatic inoculation from plants, thorns, sphagnum moss, wood splinters, hay (gardeners, farmers, florists — 'rose gardener's disease'); zoonotic from cats (S. brasiliensis)
- Common in sub-Himalayan India (Himachal, north-east), Kangra

**Q3. Clinical types?**
- Lymphocutaneous (commonest, ~75%): nodule/ulcer at inoculation site with nodules along lymphatics (sporotrichoid spread)
- Fixed cutaneous: single plaque/verrucous lesion (face, in endemic areas with prior sensitisation)
- Disseminated/extracutaneous (osteoarticular, pulmonary) in immunocompromised

**Q4. Differential diagnosis of sporotrichoid spread?**
- Mycobacterium marinum (fish tank granuloma — the closest mimic), nocardiosis, leishmaniasis, tularaemia, cat-scratch disease, blastomycosis, mycobacterial infections, sporotrichoid pyogenic infections

**Q5. Investigations?**
- Biopsy: suppurative granulomatous inflammation; organisms rare — cigar-shaped yeasts; asteroid bodies (Splendore–Hoeppli reaction around yeast)
- Culture on Sabouraud's at 25 °C (moist, cream → black colonies); conversion to yeast at 37 °C
- Sporotrichin skin test; PCR

**Q6. What are asteroid bodies and where else are they seen?**
- Eosinophilic radiating material around fungal cells — Splendore–Hoeppli phenomenon (antigen–antibody deposition)
- Also seen in sarcoidosis (in giant cells — different), botryomycosis, mycetoma, schistosomiasis, zygomycosis

**Q7. Treatment?**
- Itraconazole 200 mg/day until 2–4 weeks after lesions resolve (usually 3–6 months) — drug of choice
- Saturated solution of potassium iodide (SSKI) — cheap alternative (1 mL three times daily increasing to 4–6 mL three times daily)
- Terbinafine 500 mg twice daily; local heat (fungus cannot grow above 39 °C) in pregnancy; amphotericin B for disseminated disease

## Quick spotter facts
- Ulcerated nodule on finger with nodules along the lymphatics of the forearm — lymphocutaneous sporotrichosis

_Sources: DYP Survival Guide for PG Dermatology Exam (Other deep fungal infections — sporotrichosis); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e ch.19. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
